literal: At the end of the Wei Wuding era, he began his career as an army aide in the Secretariat.
idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era he entered service as an army aide in the Secretariat.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, his elder brother Shao granted him the separate enfeoffment as Marquis of Bacheng County.
idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate, his elder brother Shao transferred to him the separate enfeoffment as marquis of Bacheng County.

literal: Through successive promotions he rose to rank equal to the three excellencies, minister of revenue, and magistrate of Qingdu.
idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to rank equal to the three excellencies, minister of revenue, and magistrate of Qingdu.

literal: Xiaoyan had originally reached high office thanks to the residual prestige of meritorious kin; once there he grew arrogant, prodigal, and utterly without fear.
idiomatic: Xiaoyan had risen to eminence on the lingering credit of a martial clan — and once there he turned arrogant and unrestrained, afraid of nothing.

literal: Once while traveling at night he passed the house where his guest Song Xiaowang was staying and summoned the ward watchmen; when they did not come at once, he had them beaten to death.
idiomatic: Once on a night journey he passed the house where his guest Song Xiaowang was lodging and called out the ward watchmen; when they did not come at once, he had them beaten to death.

literal: He also carried on secret affairs with various adulterous women; when a husband discovered it, Xiaoyan again relied on official power and beat the man until he died.
idiomatic: He also kept secret company with adulterous women; when a husband caught him at it, Xiaoyan again leaned on his office and beat the man until he died.

literal: When the imperial gardens needed fruit trees, levies were laid on private households and Buddhist temples to supply them — but Xiaoyan had everything diverted to plant at his private residence.
idiomatic: When the palace gardens needed fruit trees, levies were laid on common households and Buddhist temples to supply them — yet Xiaoyan had the whole levy split off and planted at his private residence.

literal: When the palace halls and gardens needed stone, cart oxen were dispatched to haul it from the Zhang River — yet he diverted the carts to carry loads for himself on the return.
idiomatic: When the palace halls and gardens needed stone, cart oxen were sent to haul it from the Zhang River — and again he diverted the carts on the return trip for his own use.

literal: When all these matters became fully known, he was sent out as governor of Haizhou.
idiomatic: When every detail reached the throne, he was sent out as governor of Haizhou.

literal: Soon, because of his elder brother, he was recalled and appointed minister of justice, with income from Yangcheng Commandery, and additionally granted an opening establishment.
idiomatic: Soon, on account of his elder brother, he was recalled and made minister of justice, drawing income from Yangcheng Commandery, with an opening establishment added.

literal: He was transferred to grand minister of ceremonies, then made governor of Qi Province, and was impeached by the censorate for bribery and embezzlement.
idiomatic: He was transferred to grand minister of ceremonies, then appointed governor of Qi Province — and impeached by the censorate for bribery and embezzlement.

literal: It happened that Shizu died; he received amnesty and was pardoned.
idiomatic: It happened that Emperor Wucheng died; he was pardoned in the general amnesty.

literal: He was appointed grand minister of ceremonies, transferred to income from Henan Commandery, and promoted to minister of personnel.
idiomatic: He was made grand minister of ceremonies, transferred to income from Henan Commandery, and promoted to minister of personnel.

literal: When Zu Ting held power and planned to remove Zhao Yanshen, he brought Xiaoyan in as an ally.
idiomatic: When Zu Ting took power and plotted to remove Zhao Yanshen, he enlisted Xiaoyan as an ally.

literal: Xiaoyan was appointed acting attendant-in-ordinary, entered the inner secretariat to manage confidential affairs, was soon made full attendant-in-ordinary, and still held the post of minister of personnel.
idiomatic: Xiaoyan was made acting attendant-in-ordinary, entered the inner secretariat to handle confidential affairs, was soon confirmed in the post, and still held minister of personnel.

literal: Xiaoyan had no deep discernment and treated men unfairly; those he promoted were either bribed or old connections.
idiomatic: Xiaoyan lacked deep judgment and dealt unfairly with men — those he raised were either bought or old connections.

literal: The director of palace construction Cui Cheng suddenly spoke up before the assembly: "The minister is minister to the realm — not the Duan family's private minister!
idiomatic: Director of palace construction Cui Cheng suddenly cried out before the assembly: "The minister serves the realm — not the Duan household alone!

literal: " Xiaoyan had no reply; he could only darken his face and have Cui dismissed.
idiomatic: " Xiaoyan had no answer; he could only darken his face and have Cui sent down.

literal: Soon he was made supervisor of the Secretariat and granted extraordinary promotion.
idiomatic: Soon he was made supervisor of the Secretariat and granted extraordinary promotion.

literal: He also relied on Han Changluan to join in fabricating charges against Zu Ting.
idiomatic: He also leaned on Han Changluan to join in fabricating charges against Zu Ting.

literal: After Zu was removed, Xiaoyan was appointed vice director of the Masters of Writing on the right, still in charge of appointments; he disposed of offices as he pleased, and requests and petitions flowed in abundance.
idiomatic: After Zu was driven out, Xiaoyan was made right vice director of the Masters of Writing, still controlling appointments — disposing of offices as he pleased while petitions and favors poured in.

literal: An edict ordered the dredging of the northern moat of the capital; Xiaoyan supervised the work. Yitong of the third rank Cui Shishun, grand master of palace construction Yuan Shijiang, vice minister of the palace store Li Xiaoyu, left bureau director of the people in the Masters of Writing Xue Shuzhao, provincial aide of Sizhou Cui Longzi, vice magistrate of Qingdu Li Daolong, magistrate of Ye County Wei Changqing, magistrate of Linzhang Cui Xiang, magistrate of Cheng'an Gao Ziche, and others all served under Xiaoyan.
idiomatic: An edict ordered the dredging of the capital's northern moat, with Xiaoyan supervising the work. Yitong of the third rank Cui Shishun, grand master of palace construction Yuan Shijiang, vice minister of the palace store Li Xiaoyu, left bureau director of the people in the Masters of Writing Xue Shuzhao, provincial aide of Sizhou Cui Longzi, vice magistrate of Qingdu Li Daolong, magistrate of Ye County Wei Changqing, magistrate of Linzhang Cui Xiang, magistrate of Cheng'an Gao Ziche, and others all served under Xiaoyan.

literal: On days when he oversaw the work he set out wine and held a grand feast; the men crawled on knees and prostrated themselves, raised cups to wish him long life, or pleaded their own grievances and asked for transfer to other posts. Xiaoyan's bearing was buoyant — he took it as his proper role — and answered each as the case required, promising separate appointments.
idiomatic: On days he oversaw the work he set out wine and held a grand feast; the men crawled forward on their knees, raised cups to wish him long life, or pleaded their own grievances and asked for transfer. Xiaoyan's bearing was buoyant — he took it as his proper role — and answered each man as the case required, promising separate appointments.

literal: Wealthy merchants were often selected and promoted; even those he advanced on recommendation were all coarse, reckless, and unrestrained men.
idiomatic: Wealthy merchants were often selected and promoted; even those he advanced on recommendation were coarse, reckless, unrestrained men.

literal: Soon he was transferred to left vice director of the Masters of Writing; his extraordinary promotion and attendant-in-ordinary status remained unchanged.
idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to left vice director of the Masters of Writing; his extraordinary promotion and attendant-in-ordinary status remained unchanged.

literal: Xiaoyan was rich, noble, and extravagantly luxurious, and above all fond of women.
idiomatic: Xiaoyan was rich, noble, and extravagantly luxurious — and above all fond of women.

literal: Later he took as wife the concubine Dong of Lou Dingyuan and became utterly infatuated with her; because of this, relations inside and outside the household turned sour, accusations flew back and forth, and for the quarrel he was stripped of office and banished to Guang Province.
idiomatic: Later he took Lou Dingyuan's concubine Dong as his wife and became utterly infatuated with her; inside and outside the household turned sour, accusations flew back and forth, and for the quarrel he was stripped of office and banished to Guang Province.

literal: After the defeat at Longhua, an edict recalled him.
idiomatic: After the defeat at Longhua, an edict recalled him.

literal: Though Xiaoyan was insatiable in grasping wealth and abandoned himself to wine and women, his bearing was elegant; he gathered famous scholars, and on fine days in fair seasons he never let an hour go idle — composing poetry, summoning performers, draining every cup to the dregs.
idiomatic: Though Xiaoyan was insatiable in grasping wealth and abandoned himself to wine and women, his bearing was elegant; he gathered famous scholars, and on fine days in fair seasons he never let an hour go idle — composing poetry, summoning performers, draining every cup to the dregs.

literal: Even men from the humblest walks of life, if they had some slight skill in letters, he often brought into his guest lodges to share in the pleasure; those in poverty and distress he also sometimes gave alms.
idiomatic: Even men from the humblest walks of life, if they had some slight skill in letters, he often brought into his guest lodges to share the pleasure; those in poverty and distress he also sometimes gave alms.

literal: Public opinion again praised him for this.
idiomatic: Public opinion again praised him for this.

literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou and was granted opening-establishment honors equal to the grand general; later he was granted supreme opening establishment.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered Zhou and was granted opening-establishment honors equal to the grand general; later he was granted supreme opening establishment.

literal: The historian says: Duan Rong, by weight of marriage kinship, met the tide of the times; in fields where merit is reckoned, he is worth naming.
idiomatic: The historian says: Duan Rong, by weight of marriage kinship, met the tide of the times — in fields where merit is reckoned, he is worth naming.

literal: Shao brightly assisted seven rulers and enlarged the family estate; whenever he went out he held the outer command, or was entrusted with the capital in his absence — and in a court of suspicion he lived out his years to the full.
idiomatic: Shao brightly assisted seven rulers and enlarged the family estate; whenever he went out he held the outer command, or was entrusted with the capital in his absence — and in a court of suspicion he lived out his years to the full.

literal: Just when frontier beacons were often alight, that Qi should have such a supreme general — can it have been mere chance?
idiomatic: Just when frontier beacons were often alight, that Qi should have such a supreme general — can it have been mere chance?

literal: Surely it was because he kept ambition from pride in merit, kept fame from outrunning reality, did not rule men by raw power, and did not seize the moment by cunning stratagem — who, then, could have overturned his bowl?
idiomatic: Surely it was because he kept ambition from pride in merit, kept fame from outrunning reality, did not rule men by raw power, and did not seize the moment by cunning stratagem — who, then, could have overturned his bowl?

literal: The saying runs, "To follow one's nature is called the Way" — is this not its proof?
idiomatic: The saying runs, "To follow one's nature is called the Way" — is this not its proof?

literal: The encomium says: Rong opened the springhead; Shao enlarged the gate.
idiomatic: The encomium says: Rong opened the springhead; Shao enlarged the gate.

literal: Rank rose through merit; renown rested on virtue.
idiomatic: Rank rose through merit; renown rested on virtue.

literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
